intro: This monorepo holds three apps: the web wallet (`apps/web`), the user API (`apps/user`), and the mobile wallet (`apps/native`). One install serves all three. Start only the apps that you need.
prerequisites: Node.js 20 and Corepack (Corepack comes with Node.js). CI uses Node 20. Corepack installs the Yarn version that `package.json` names (Yarn 4.9.4).
Docker, to run PostgreSQL for the user API.
For the mobile app: an Android emulator or an Android device.

steps.title: Run the tests
steps.text: This runs the unit tests of the user API. The web app has Cypress component tests: `yarn cypress-component-test`. CI runs the user API integration and e2e tests with Keycloak secrets that are not public.

steps.title: Start the web app
steps.text: The web app opens on http://localhost:3000. The example file points the wallet API at the Greenstand dev server. The web app reads `apps/web/.env`; the README copies the file to `apps/user/.env` instead.

steps.title: Start PostgreSQL
steps.text: The user API needs a PostgreSQL database for its message queue. This local database accepts connections without a password.

steps.title: Start the user API
steps.text: The user API listens on http://localhost:8080. The Swagger UI is at http://localhost:8080/swagger. At this commit, the user API does not read `DATABASE_URL` from `.dev.env`: without the `export`, it stops with `error in connecting to DB`. Registration and login call the Greenstand Keycloak server. Ask a maintainer for the `PRIVATE_KEYCLOAK_*` values in `apps/user/.dev.env`.

steps.title: Start the mobile app
steps.text: Metro starts on http://localhost:8081. Press `a` to open the app in an Android emulator. To build and install a native debug app, follow `apps/native/README.md`.
